The current [Web Editor](https://editor.godotengine.org/releases/4.3.stable/godot.editor.html) from the official website does not crash.

I couldn't reproduce it with those steps, but I did manage to reproduce it by starting with the parent ON and the child OFF, then:
- Turning child ON
- Turning child OFF
- Turning parent OFF, which crashes to desktop

The issue is that viewports don't have their scenarios updated when an ancestor they're relying on for their world (and thus scenario) updates to a different world. This is a problem both when deleting that world, which causes use after frees (this error message is one of those cases), and when switching to a different world without freeing the original one, which does not crash the game but does mean that the child viewport will not correctly inherit the new update. 

In the above repro steps, for example, toggling the child on and off causes it to grab its parent's scenario. Turning the parent off then removes the last reference to that world, freeing it. The child then attempts to access invalid memory in _render_scene as a result.

The fix seems pretty straightforward, this just updates the child viewports' scenarios when the parent world changes. Setting the scenario to null on the viewports before a potential free on the world is also necessary because the `viewport_set_scenario` function attempts to perform clean up on the old scenario.
